cohort: The study analyzed a hypothetical cohort of patients undergoing a cesarean delivery in Brazil.
finding: Intermittent pneumatic compression was found to be cost-effective compared to no prophylaxis and dominated low-molecular-weight heparin, with lower costs and improved effectiveness.
mod_finding: Intermittent pneumatic compression could be a cost-effective option and more appropriate than low-molecular-weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis specifically for cesarean delivery in Brazil.
